labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE, no X: FS-UAE 3.2.35 (its OWN copy at assets/amix/fsuae-native, built from the merged source with fsuae-slirp-hostfwd.patch, FSUAE_STATION=amix) runs an Amiga 3000 (68030+MMU, Kickstart 2.04 r37.175) with an A2410 TIGA board headless (no DISPLAY, no GL), publishing shm frames (SH_CAPTURE=shm) via the shared launcher stations/fsuae-native/x11-runtime.sh (a1000/a3000/amigaos35's launcher). No QEMU/QMP, no exec channel. POINTER unchanged by this conversion: ABSOLUTE via the GUEST's own X server (SH_INPUT_BACKEND=x11test + SH_X11TEST_MOTION=warp + SH_X11WARP_DISPLAY=127.0.0.1:72), because the UAE mousehack is an AmigaOS trap AMIX never registers -- host motion arrives at the guest's own X -tiga server via a loopback-only slirp redirect 127.0.0.1:6072 -> 10.0.2.15:6000 (FSUAE_NATIVE_EXTRA_ARGS on the shared launcher; the daemon warps with XWarpPointer and reads back with XQueryPointer, buttons/keys still ride XTEST with each edge held until the warp is confirmed). Single injector: never push motion at this guest by another path. Golden (unified 2026-09-01) carries the colour session, /etc/inet/hosts amix=10.0.2.15 + slirphost=10.0.2.2 (rc.inet brings aen0 up; NO default route), and xhost +slirphost in both /etc/kh-xsession and /etc/kh-xsession.mono. Reset=relaunch: cold boot of a fresh work HDF copied from disk/amix-system.hdf.golden; no statefile. Framebuffer-proven 2026-09-01 on the shipping (Xvfb) binary at 1024x768: readback exact and sprite on target at 16 points incl. all four corners, residual 0 px; click and keys proven by guest response (docs/guests/amix.md); the shm/no-X conversion (2026-09-09) is repo-side only, re-verification on the shared launcher NOT YET DONE live.

render.stationsManifestPrelude: # amix — host-native FS-UAE 3.2.35 (A3000, 68030+MMU, Kickstart 2.04) -> Amiga UNIX (AMIX) 2.1, System V R4 with the OPEN LOOK desktop, in COLOUR on an A2410 (1024x768, 8-bit PseudoColor, selected by starting AMIX's X server with -tiga). The chipset X server is depth 1, so monochrome 640x512 is the fallback and is one flag away (/etc/kh-xsession.mono in the guest). Absolute 1:1 pointer via x11warp into the guest's own X server over a loopback-bound slirp redirect.

pointer.device: guest X server (X -tiga on the A2410; motion via loopback slirp redirect) + amiga-mouse/keyboard over XTEST (buttons, keys)

museum.lineage: Commodore Amiga / AT&T UNIX System V Release 4 (ported by Commodore)
museum.arch: Motorola 68030 @ 25 MHz with MMU + 68882 FPU, A2410 graphics board (Amiga 3000)
eraSoftware: X11R4 and the AT&T OPEN LOOK toolkit (OLIT)
museum.periodBrowser: none — this station is offline, and in 1992 a Unix machine's network was uucp and Usenet: AMIX ships C News, NNTP and an SVR4 TCP/IP stack, not a browser
museum.blurb: Commodore licensed AT&T's System V Release 4 and shipped it on the Amiga 3000, wearing OPEN LOOK — the desktop AT&T specified for SVR4, and the one Motif beat — instead of Workbench. Nobody ever published how many sold. This one has the A2410 graphics board fitted, so it runs OPEN LOOK in colour: the option that took the price from $4,998 to $7,713.
museum.notes: Host-native without X (converted 2026-09-09, repo-side): FS-UAE 3.2.35 (its OWN copy at assets/amix, built with fsuae-slirp-hostfwd.patch) runs an Amiga 3000 (68030+MMU, Kickstart 2.04 r37.175) with an A2410 TIGA board headless, publishing shm frames via the shared launcher stations/fsuae-native/x11-runtime.sh -- no Xvfb. The pointer is unchanged: absolute through the guest's own X -tiga server over a loopback slirp redirect (127.0.0.1:6072 -> 10.0.2.15:6000), buttons/keys over XTEST into that same guest X server. Reset=relaunch: cold boot of a fresh work HDF from disk/amix-system.hdf.golden, no statefile. Distinct from amigaos35/a3000 (Amiga desktop OS, mousehack pointer) -- AMIX is the machine's UNIX side, sharing the a3000/amiga.md lineage. See docs/guests/amix.md.

network.note: A2065 on FS-UAE slirp, used ONLY for the pointer: a loopback-bound redirect 127.0.0.1:6072 -> guest 10.0.2.15:6000 lets the daemon drive the guest's X server. Fail-closed: the guest has no default route (only 10.0.2.0/24), the redirect binds 127.0.0.1, and there is no retronet tap. Not a retronet join; a web-plane join remains a follow-up.

Framebuffer-proven sweep in docs/guests/amix.md.
